title: Translation becomes infrastructure
technology: Japanese and English interfaces, search, metadata
governingQuestion: What must cross languages before a collection can cross markets?

publication.author: Rayven-Nikkita Collins
publication.status: publication-ready text; human recording, permissions, specialist and RN owner-final gates remain

essay.headline: Translation becomes infrastructure
essay.opening: International circulation begins with translation infrastructure.

sections.heading: Then
sections.copy: The organizer operates Japanese and English interfaces across programme, brands, topics and organizational information.

sections.heading: Now
sections.copy: The interface carries names, categories, access conditions and venue information across languages, but translation depth varies by record.

sections.heading: Next / limit
sections.copy: No reviewed public record documents one season-wide translation workflow, glossary, error process or accessibility standard.

essay.closing: Tokyo’s technical identity is not one gadget. It is the chain of interfaces that decides what can enter, travel, translate, trade and remain.
